text: rule_package_version carries a state, a valid-from date, the approver, the generated DRL and a SHA-256 of the stored artifact, and a compiled version is served as a claim-checked artifact with its version label and checksum; the further physical columns are taken from the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary at implementation.
why: The TSD defines decision_log_entry and approval field by field and gives no field list for the four rule tables, and the promotion, the serving and the checksum refusal cannot be built or tested without a state, a date, an approver and a content hash.
read: TSD P7 T3.1; FSD P7 AC-P7-007-01 and AC-ALT-P7-007-02; legacy RWB-E1-020 sections 11 and 13; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-04
confirm: P7 solution architect and the owner of RWB-PLT-E1072-CON at the model contract review
impact: Column names and payload shape only; the states, the promotion time, the checksum refusal and every criterion stay unchanged

text: The ALLOCATION row that matches MORTGAGE in BKK and targets queue MTG-BKK-CO is cited in this story by its legacy rule ID ALLOC-014, the FSD label ALLOC-MTG-BKK-01 is treated as another name of the same row, and the rule ID on an entry is always copied from the record as it arrives.
why: The legacy story and the module FSD name the same row of the same package version differently, and the story has to cite one label in its criteria and examples.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-020 AC1, AC2 and BR1; FSD P7 AC-P7-002-01; Template and Rules R3
confirm: P7 business analyst and the reference data administrator at the package load
impact: A data value in a package row; no code, criterion or record shape changes

text: A decision record carries the business date as a record attribute and the queue identifier and the owner identifier as named members of the actions payload, and the ledger deduplicates on the event identifier first and on the case and business date second.
why: One entry per case and business date and the display of the queue and owner of an allocation both need values the sources do not place in the record.
read: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-002-03; legacy RWB-E1-020 section 12
confirm: P7 and P3 contract owners at the decision-record contract review
impact: Field names and the dedupe key only; the one-entry rule and every criterion stay unchanged

text: MSG-P7-009 is answered as an RFC 9457 refusal that names the offending field and carries no fixed text, a broken chain on a page is shown as a warning naming the entry and is reported to Compliance the same day, and the per-entry field that carries the chain result is named chainVerified.
why: The FSD fixes the message ID and the named field but quotes no text, and the read needs a field name for the chain result.
read: FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-002-01, AC-EXC-P7-002-05, AC-BG-P7-006-01; TSD P7 T7 NFR-035; legacy RWB-E1-020 section 14
confirm: P7 business analyst and the Compliance officer at the message catalogue review
impact: Wording and a field name only; the refusal, the same-day report and the visible break do not change

text: A compiled rule package version is served to the owning service on the service base as GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-models/{packageCode}/{version} under a model-owner service identity, and the operation is added to the P7 row of the Ownership Map and to the API Specification.
why: DP-04 places the packages here and the evaluation there, the owning service must obtain the artifact from this service, and the Ownership Map carries no such operation.
read: Ownership Map v1 P7 provided operations; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-04; FSD P7 A2.7; TSD P7 T-A.1
confirm: P7 solution architect and the Ownership Map owner at the next API Specification version
impact: One path and one row of the Ownership Map; the version-in-force and checksum rules and every criterion stay unchanged
